question: In which of the places was Arya Samaj founded?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Arya Samaj was founded by **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** in 1875 in Bombay.
 
• The main objective of Arya Samaj was to reform Hinduism by promoting **Vedic principles** and opposing superstitions and social evils.
 
• Swami Dayanand Saraswati advocated the philosophy of "**Back to the Vedas**" to revive the spiritual essence of ancient Hindu scriptures.
 
• The Arya Samaj actively worked toward **abolishing caste discrimination** and promoting education, especially for women.
 
• The organization also played a significant role in India's **social and cultural awakening** during the 19th and 20th centuries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swami Dayanand Saraswati**

 
 
• Born in 1824, Swami Dayanand was a Hindu spiritual leader and social reformer.
 
• He authored the book "**Satyarth Prakash**" (The Light of Truth), which laid the foundation for Arya Samaj's principles.
 
• He opposed idol worship and rituals that had no basis in the Vedic scriptures.
 
 
 
• **Key Principles of Arya Samaj**
 
 
• Belief in the authority of the Vedas as the ultimate source of knowledge.
 
• Promotion of monotheism and rejection of polytheism and idol worship.
 
• Encouragement of universal education, social equality, and women's empowerment.
 
 
 
• **Educational Contributions**
 
 
• Arya Samaj established schools and colleges, such as the **DAV (Dayanand Anglo Vedic) institutions**, which are renowned for their emphasis on value-based education.
 
• Promoted the teaching of Sanskrit and Vedic literature.
 
 
 
• **Social Reform Activities**
 
 
• Opposition to untouchability and promotion of social equality.
 
• Campaign against child marriage and promotion of widow remarriage.
 
• Arya Samaj played a significant role in India's freedom struggle by fostering national pride and cultural revival.
